about: The grammar deinflection.json is generated from (scripts/deinflection/generate_rules.py), with UniDic's conjugation data supplying every ending. Hand-reviewed: each row is a textbook fact or a recorded decision. Grammar names are the ones deinflection.json uses: v5, v1, vk, vs, adj-i for dictionary forms; te, ta, nu, masu for steps inside a chain. Every row names the group its rules go in: the group name is what the lookup sheet captions a form with (InflectionFormNames) and what the segmenter recognises stem recovery and the noun suffix by.

attachments.note: godan potential (書ける): UniDic lists these as verbs of their own
volitional/conjecture む, written ん (行かん, 見ん)
literary causative, modern ichidan (泣かしめる)
past, written し before a noun (過ぎし日)
perfective たり, not the representative たり (書きたる)
perfective ぬ (散りぬ); the negative ぬ takes the 未然形, and an ichidan's are the same
perfective/continuous り after a godan え-form (咲ける, 書けり)
classical 已然形 + ば (出づれば)

voicing.about: た/て/たり after ん, and after a ガ行 イ音便 (泳いだ), are voiced.

stemCompounds.about: Verbs and auxiliaries joined to a verb's 連用形 (読みつづける, 食べすぎる, 書きやすい), folded into one segment with the second part named as the helper.

teHelpers.about: Helper verbs after a verb's て-form folded into one segment (持っている). Only いる, いく/ゆく and くれる: Tatoeba, JMdict and MeCab write て | しまう, て | くる, て | ある … as two tokens, and so does the segmenter (2026-10-03: folding them all cut 7 gold tokens in held2k and gave してあれ | ほど). てゆく/ていく and てくれる fold by the user's own decision (named cases 飛び込んでゆく, 歌い続けてゆく; the hand-written benefactive rules). The contractions below fuse て with the helper in writing, so they do fold.

contractions.note: ていた with the い dropped (持ってた)

standaloneForms.about: Forms used on their own, by the group the lookup sheet names them with. Groups whose name contains "stem" are bare-stem recovery, which the segmenter treats as such (Segmenter.surfaceIsOutrankedByConjugation).

auxiliaryConjugations.about: Auxiliaries whose own forms get rules, with the grammar a word ending in them has. Only their standalone forms (standaloneForms: なきゃ, ましょう): their other forms take further auxiliaries, which the attachment rules cover (ない conjugates like an adjective; ます takes た/ぬ itself, まし + た). A rule for every form would admit fragments like なけれ, cutting なければならない. A row may name further forms that do end a word (forms, with formsWhy); a classical auxiliary (classicalForms) gets all of its classical forms, less the measured exceptions in omitted.

ぬ.formsWhy: ざる before a noun or を (望まざる, 許されざる, 言わざるを得ない) ends a word; it is not a fragment like なけれ

classicalVerbs.about: Classical verb conjugations whose forms get rules, by UniDic conjugation family, with the grammar their rules end on. The grammar names JMdict's tags (v2*-s shimo-nidan, v2*-k kami-nidan; ConjugationClass maps them), so a chain only reaches an entry JMdict tags that way: 出ずる → 出ず (v2d-s). Only the forms no modern verb shares: the 連体形 (出づる, 過ぐる) on its own, and the 已然形 with ば/ど/ども (出づれば). The 未然形 and 連用形 (出で, 消え) are modern ichidan stems too, and a rule for them would list the archaic verb beside every modern form. All rules go in classicalGroup, so the segmenter prices them as classical steps.

auxiliaryCoverage.about: Every auxiliary (助動詞) UniDic lists must be covered by a row above or named here with the reason it gets no rules; the generator fails the build otherwise (check_auxiliary_coverage).

omittedPatterns.about: Generated rules dropped by pattern: UniDic forms that are real but wrong for this purpose. Applied to generated rules only, never to deinflection-extras.json. Decided 2026-10-03 after reviewing every generated rule the hand-written file lacked.
